explanation: For nonzero solutions, set z=y^{-2}. Then z'=-2y^{-3}y', so the equation becomes z'-2z=2x. Using the integrating factor e^{-2x} gives z=Ke^{2x}-x-1/2. Thus y=±sqrt(2/(Ce^{2x}-2x-1)), option c, on intervals where the denominator is positive. The equation also has the separate solution y=0.
